title: Effect of resveratrol on lipid profile: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis on randomized clinical trials - ScienceDirect
abstract:
We conclude that resveratrol does not change lipid profile concentration. Confirmation of this conclusion will require more studies exclusively on dyslipidemic patients in which the intake of lipid lowering agents is among the exclusion criteria.
Despite the notion that resveratrol can significantly reduce plasma lipids, the result of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) on resveratrol effect and the serum lipid profile are contradictory. Our objective was to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis on randomized clinical trials (RCTs) and assess the effect of resveratrol on lipids.
RCTs that assessed resveratrol effects on lipid profile among adult participants were chosen. Treatment effects were considered as weighted mean difference (WMD) and the corresponding standard error (SE) in concentrations of serum lipids. To estimate the overall summary effect, we used random-effects model. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (No. CRD42017072365). This meta-analysis was performed on twenty-one trials.
Meanwhile, several new RCTs on resveratrol effect on lipid parameters have become available; these used higher doses of resveratrol and longer duration of intervention to find. Whether new RCTs changed the result of previous meta-analysis was unknown. Hence, we performed an update systematic review to summarize the RCTs data reported in fifteen articles after year 2013 exploring the effect of resveratrol on serum lipid profile and conducted a meta-analysis.
We conclude that resveratrol does not change lipid profile concentration. Confirmation of this conclusion will require more studies exclusively on dyslipidemic patients in which the intake of lipid lowering agents is among the exclusion criteria. ... A: Meta-analysis of the effect of resveratrol supplementation on total cholesterol.
